title: One Field, New Type
goal: Wrap a number so the compiler stops treating it as just a number.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 1 Afternoon: User-Defined Types (Tuple Structs)

hints: The code builds one with `Meters(3)` and reads it with `.0`.
`Meters(3)` hands the field a whole number.
explanation: A struct written `struct Meters(i32);` is a tuple struct. Its field has no name, so you build it like a function call and read it with `.0`. The named form `{ value: i32 }` has to be built with `Meters { value: 3 }` instead, so the calls here stop compiling. Choosing `f64` breaks too, because `Meters(3)` hands it a whole number. This one-field wrapper is called a newtype. It is how you stop a length being mistaken for a weight. Both are numbers, but they are no longer the same type.
